content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/diogenes/.claude/plugins/cache/typesafe-ai/typesafe/0.5.7/skills/typesafe-ai

# Build with TypeSafe

TypeSafe makes units of AI intelligence usable like programming primitives: small
judgments you can compose into larger capabilities. Its **System One models** return
fast, focused judgments that software can consume directly. **Jev** is TypeSafe's
flagship and first System One model. It understands natural language and returns
typed answers and probabilities rather
than generating text or reasoning explanations. Code owns the workflow; the model
supplies programmable common sense where ordinary code needs semantic understanding.

## Read the live docs

**The live TypeSafe docs are the source of truth. Read them as part of the task.**
This skill gives direction; the docs carry current concepts, prompting guidance,
API contracts, SDK usage, models, limits, and worked examples.

- Start with the [documentation index](https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt) to discover
  relevant pages and cookbooks. Use targeted reads rather than loading the entire site.
- Mintlify serves Markdown by appending `.md` to a page path, for example
  [how to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md).
  Follow links from the index; convert extensionless documentation page links to
  `.md` when useful. Resolve relative links against `https://docs.typesafe.ai`.
- Before writing an integration, read the current API or chosen SDK page and the
  question guidance relevant to the design. For a new workflow, also inspect the
  closest cookbook: it often shows a better decomposition than a generic classifier.
- If the index is unavailable, use the direct links below or the site's navigation.
  If Markdown fetching fails, try the normal page. If live access is unavailable,
  use available local docs or installed SDK types, state that limitation, and avoid
  inventing version-dependent details.

| Task | Start here; follow the relevant details |
| --- | --- |
| Understand the programming model | [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md), [building guide](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md) |
| Explore what to build | [Use-case map](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/use-case-map.md), then relevant cookbooks from the index |
| Prepare inputs and questions | [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md), [primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives.md), then the chosen primitive's page |
| Decide how to handle uncertainty | [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md) |
| Write API code | [HTTP API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api.md), [Python SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python.md), or [JavaScript SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript.md) |
| Update an older integration | [Migration guide](https://docs.typesafe.ai/migrating-to-v1.md) and the installed SDK's current reference |

## Find the useful shape

Start from the behavior the user wants: what will the application show, select,
change, or hand off? Work backward to the judgments it needs. Keep known rules,
calculations, exact lookups, and execution in code. Preserve the user's chosen stack
and scope; add TypeSafe where semantic understanding helps.

When brainstorming or choosing an architecture, consider more than classification.
The patterns below are starting points: combine primitives around the user's goal,
including ideas that do not fit an established recipe.

- **Route and fill known arguments.** A request can select a handler and its typed
  parameters. Ask useful branch-specific questions up front and consume only the
  relevant answers. Explore [function calling](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/function_calling.md)
  and [speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md).
- **Select instead of generate.** Find candidate values or source spans in code,
  use a judgment to select the intended one, then copy or normalize it. Code can
  also assemble source text into a formatted document or reading guide. Explore
  [value extraction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/pre_parsed_value_extraction_cookbook.md)
  and [structure recovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoformat.md).
- **Find and judge evidence.** Retrieve candidates, compare their relevance to a
  query, and select useful context. Explore [reranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md)
  and [hierarchical classification](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/hierarchical_classification.md).
- **Turn judgments into reusable data.** Score dimensions once, then let code or
  user controls change weights, thresholds, rankings, and views. With labeled
  outcomes, those signals can become classical ML features. Explore
  [composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) and
  [feature discovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md).
- **Verify and escalate.** Check specific claims or fields against their evidence;
  send uncertain or failing cases to a person or reasoning model. Explore
  [citation checks](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/citation_check.md) and
  [extraction cascades](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/sde_cascade.md).
- **Respond to changing state.** Code can retain goals and observations while fresh
  judgments guide the next bounded step. Keep inferred state distinct from observed
  facts, and check freshness before applying a result to a changed situation.

For open-ended requests, offer the few directions that best serve the user's goal
and recommend a starting point. For a concrete request, choose the relevant pattern
and build; a brainstorm is not a mandatory detour.

## Design the judgments

Choose by what the answer means, then read the relevant primitive page:

| Need | Primitive | Important distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One of a defined set | [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md) | Picks one option; its distribution compares competing options |
| Whether a condition holds | [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul.md) | Probability of yes; no separate confidence; use one per label when several may apply |
| Degree along a described dimension | [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score.md) | Probability-weighted position on ordered levels; use comparable per-item Scores for graded ranking |

Give each question enough relevant **state** to answer: source text, identities,
relationships, policies, and current facts. Prefer named JSON fields when context
has several parts. Put the judgment in **instructions** and define its possible
answers in **criteria**. Question IDs are for code and are not sent to the model;
include complete meaning in the question. Reference nested state with backticked
paths such as `ticket.messages[0].text`.

Ask one narrow, coherent judgment per question. Split independently useful dimensions,
without destroying the relationship being judged. A bounded action selection or
contextual interpretation is valid; atomic does not mean literal fact extraction
or a one-sentence limit. Strings work for simple questions. Use structured objects
or arrays when definitions, contrasts, exclusions, or examples clarify instructions
or criteria. Score levels must describe concrete situations and stand on their own.

Keep the needed answers available. Include a no-match outcome when nothing may fit;
use a separate presence judgment when it is independently useful. For source-value
selection, check candidate coverage: the model cannot choose an omitted value.

## Compose and verify

**Ask independent questions over the same state together**, including useful
speculative questions. They run in parallel and cannot see one another's answers.
State each speculative premise explicitly; code consumes the applicable answers.
A second request is warranted when an earlier answer is needed to fetch evidence,
construct new state, or determine the next options. Extra questions still use tokens;
measure actual request budgets, cost, and end-to-end latency.

Use probabilities and confidence to guide behavior, with thresholds evaluated on
the user's data and consequences. Choice/Score confidence summarizes distribution
concentration, not overall workflow correctness or permission to act. A Noul near
0.5 means similar probability for yes and no, not medium intensity. Several
acceptable alternatives can also spread probability; low confidence need not
invalidate a harmless preference choice. Ignore uncertainty on unused branches.

Keep policy explicit and raw judgments reusable. Weighted scores suit compensating
preferences; an “any serious violation” rule needs separate conditions. Changing a
weight or display filter need not rerun inference when evidence and question meanings
are unchanged. Typed output guarantees the interface, not truth. System One models
are trained for calibrated decisions; validate their performance in the target domain.

Test representative cases and the resulting application behavior. For failures,
inspect the exact state, questions, candidates, answers, composition, and observed
outcome. Separate missing evidence, model errors, code errors, and service failures.
Treat cookbook thresholds and demo results as examples to evaluate, not universal
rules or permanent model limitations. Keep API credentials server-side in web apps.

I can't reproduce the changelog verbatim because of the quoting limits, but here is a close summary with short exact quotes.

## v0.7.0 (2026-10-14)

**Breaking changes**
- The minimum runtime is now Node.js 22 ("require Node.js 22 or newer").
- Request payload types are no longer exported.

**Features (image/multimodal/asset)**
- **Images (experimental):** These are enabled via the `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true` header. You create them with `image()` or `Image.fromBase64()`. They can go in `state`, question instructions, or criteria. You can embed them in text using `withAssets` / `withAssets.join`, or refer to them by custom names in `assets`.
- **`box` questions:** These "locate what their instructions describe in an image" and are used with the `jev-preview` model.
- **Compression:** Request bodies of 1 KiB or larger are zstd-compressed on Node.js 22.15+. You can opt out with `compression: false`.

**Bug fixes**
- Null token counts in usage are now permitted.
- Additional request validation checks were added.
- Invalid requests now reject the returned promise rather than throwing.
- Score criteria lists constructed at runtime are accepted.
- An unhandled rejection on Node.js 22 was fixed. It happened when a request timed out or was aborted mid-body.

## v0.6.0 (2026-09-15)

**Breaking change**
- `Score.criteria` is now an ordered sequence, not a dictionary keyed by integers.

## v0.5.7 (2026-09-11)

- This was the first public release of the TypeSafe JavaScript/TypeScript SDK. Docs: https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/js-sdk

result.output:
# TypeSafe Jev Models: Summary

**Endpoint:** All models are served through `POST /v1/systemone`. The `model` field in the request chooses which one runs.

## Current models

| | Jev 1.14 | Jev 1.13 |
|---|---|---|
| Model ID | `jev-1.14.0` | `jev-1.13.0` |
| Price | $42 per billion tokens ($0.042 per million) | Same |
| Context | 64k per request / 32k per question | Same |
| Input | Text only | Text only |

- Jev 1.14 is the newest release, available starting October 14, 2026.
- **Pricing:** You pay only for input tokens. "Output tokens are free."

## Images and Box
- **Images:** The page does not mention image support. It lists text as the only input. Audio and video are explicitly unsupported and must be converted to text or structured fields first.
- **Box:** The page does not mention Box at all.

## Context length
- **Per-request limit:** the `state` plus all questions combined.
- **Per-question limit:** the `state` plus any single question.
- There is no cap on the number of questions, as long as the request fits both limits.
- **Long context:** This is off by default and works on both versions. To enable it, add the header `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true` to each request. Both limits then rise to 262k tokens.
  - The per-token price stays the same.
  - The docs warn it is "slower and less accurate than staying within the default limits."

## Aliases and how they resolve

| Alias | Resolves to | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `jev-latest` | `jev-1.13.0` | The newest stable, official release. It is the SDK default and is used in the doc examples. |
| `jev-preview` | `jev-1.14.0` | The newest release of any kind, including preview builds. |

- Aliases move when new versions ship, so results can change without any code changes on your side.
- Each response's `model` field reports the exact versioned ID that answered.
- If you have tuned confidence thresholds, pin a versioned ID instead of an alias.

## Deprecation
The page gives no deprecation details or timelines.

## Other notes
- **Listing models:** `GET /v1/models` currently returns only the aliases. Versioned IDs are still accepted in requests even though they are not listed.
- **Rate limits:** Limits are set per organization, in tokens per second and requests per second. Exceeding them returns a 429 error, and the SDKs retry automatically with backoff.
- **Customization:** There is no fine-tuning. You adapt Jev to your domain through the `state`, `instructions`, and `criteria` fields.
- **Language:** English works best. Other languages, including CJK scripts, work less well.
- **Data:** Jev is not trained on customer data. Zero data retention is available for enterprise customers.

result.output:
# Jev-1.13 Weak Spots

1. **Literal reading.** The model takes wording at face value and misses the intent.
   *Mitigation:* Spell out the precise condition and put edge cases in the criteria. If interpretation can't be avoided, "split it into two literal questions and combine them in code."

2. **Math and numbers.** "Jev is not a calculator."
   - **Counting:** Tallies of characters, terms or list items are unreliable, and errors grow with size. *Mitigation:* Count in code, or ask one yes/no question per item and add up the results yourself.
   - **Numeric representations:** Hex or RGB values do worse than English names, and closeness between values isn't judged reliably. *Mitigation:* Convert in code and pass "the computed number or a named bucket."
   - **Score math:** Expectations can't be used to recover exact magnitudes between levels. *Mitigation:* Use scores only for threshold checks.

3. **Dates and times.** Ordering, gaps and window checks are unreliable, especially with mixed formats or relative references. *Mitigation:* Have the model extract date parts as a Choice that includes a "not stated" option, then do all comparisons in code.

4. **Indirection.** Double negatives and multi-hop questions lower accuracy. *Mitigation:* Phrase instructions plainly and refer to the relevant state fields by name.

5. **Large, irrelevant state.** Extra content distracts the model ("context rot") and makes errors harder to trace. *Mitigation:* Filter in code first and send only the necessary fields. A Noul can also screen for relevance.

6. **Adversarial content.** Injected or misleading text in the state can shift answers. *Mitigation:* Make the criteria explicit and test thoroughly before a wide rollout.

7. **Contradictory instructions and criteria.** An example is mapping `true` to "no." *Mitigation:* Treat the criteria "as an extension of the instruction" and keep the wording aligned.

8. **Choice option order.** The model tends to favor the first option. *Mitigation:* Shuffle the options and check that the answer stays the same.

9. **Generation.** The model isn't built to produce text, and chaining Choices to force it is slow and works poorly. *Mitigation:* Get candidates from regex or a generative model, then let Jev pick one through a Choice.

The page's closing reminder also warns against putting several judgments into one question.

## Image Concerns

None of these weak spots concern images. The page never mentions images, OCR, counting objects in pictures, or comparing images.

- **Counting** refers only to text: characters, terms and list items.
- **Colors** come up only as hex or RGB values versus English names, not as pixels or visual content.

input.prompt: Quote exactly what the page says about context length: "64k per request / 32k per question" — what counts toward each (state, instructions, criteria, images), whether the per-request limit is the sum over all questions or the shared state, and what happens when exceeded. Also quote anything about how multiple questions share the state (is state processed once or per question).

result.output:
# Context length on the TypeSafe Models page

**The limits as written**

The table lists context length for both Jev 1.14 and Jev 1.13 as "64k per-request / 32k per-question". The page uses hyphens in these terms.

**What counts toward each limit**

- Per-request: "the `state` plus all questions combined."
- Per-question: "the `state` plus any one question."
- The page does not list what makes up a "question." It never says whether `instructions` or `criteria` count separately. Those fields do appear inside question objects in the example, so they likely count as part of the question, but this isn't stated.
- **Images:** The page doesn't mention them. Input is listed only as "Text," and it says Jev "does not accept audio or video."

**Is the per-request limit a sum over questions or based on shared state?**

The wording "the `state` plus all questions combined" suggests the state is counted once, plus the total of all questions. It does not suggest the state is counted once per question. The page doesn't confirm this arithmetic directly.

Related lines:
- "There is no separate limit on the number of questions in a request."
- "Any number of questions is allowed as long as the request fits both limits."

**How questions share the state**

"Jev ingests the `state` once and evaluates every question against it in parallel."

**What happens when a limit is exceeded**

The page doesn't say. The only error it describes is `429 Too Many Requests`, and that applies to rate limits, not context overflow. The alternative it offers is the long-context header, `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true`:
- "With the header, the per-request context and the per-question context are both 262k tokens."
- Long context "is slower and less accurate than staying within the default limits."

### Generate Assets

```bash
# Generate asset suite for a persona
baste generate cyberbotanist

### Cultural Experiences

Link images, screenshots, logos, and references to personas to capture the cultural DNA behind design decisions.

```bash
# Show cultural references for a persona
baste culture cyberbotanist

# Add cultural references from images
baste culture cyberbotanist ~/Pictures/cultural/hero-ref.png ~/Pictures/cultural/palette-inspiration.jpg

```

Cultural references are embedded in the design system history and exported with `.baste` files, so the "why" behind every design decision travels with the design.

### Export / Share / Import


Browse to `http://localhost:8080` to create, edit, and manage personas through a visual interface.

## Configuration File

`baste.config.json`:

```json
{
  "outputDir": "./assets/output",
  "personaDir": "./personas",
  "evaluator": {

## Programmatic API
```

- **Portable**: Single JSON file

- **Versioned**: Full history graph included

- **Tool-agnostic**: Works with OpenPencil, any CLI, Lix-aware systems

### How Jev judges

With `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` set, [Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai) judges every QD candidate and final asset. It now
looks at them, using TypeSafe's image preview ([images](https://docs.typesafe.ai/images.md), opt-in header
`TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images`):

| Jev sees | As | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| The candidate | The rendered image; an SVG on light and dark grounds at 64, 32 and 16 px; six frames of a video | The five scores, from pixels instead of the prompt |
| The persona's world | Up to four pictures: moodboard pins, `baste culture` images, a decomposed site's share image and palette | Persona alignment against what the world looks like |
| The suite | The latest finished asset of each purpose (up to four) | Coherence with what was actually rendered |
| Your ratings | Up to three upvoted and three downvoted assets of the same kind, as pictured criteria | A taste judgment that moves persona alignment by up to ±0.1 |

From the same request, Jev also reads the QD archive's three axes (colour temperature, density, rendering) off
the image, replacing the keyword guesses that placed candidates before. For images and loops, it checks for text laid over the picture: a caption, watermark or interface label rejects the asset at 0.8.
Signs and lettering in the scene are allowed. For loops, it reads the frames for motion (which of the four motion
languages they show, whether the last frame flows into the first, and how much the movement competes with
interface content) and turns misses into `improvements` without rejecting the loop.

Video frames need `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` on `PATH`; WebP and GIF stills use them too. Without them, those assets
are judged on their prompt. Nothing is resized server-side, so Baste fits every image inside TypeSafe's limits
(PNG or JPEG, 280–1568 px a side) before upload. If TypeSafe refuses an image request (`400` or `413`), the same
asset is judged again as text, and its result carries the `vision-refused` tag. `--text-judge`, or
`"vision": false` in the evaluator config, keeps every judgment text-only. Hosted Not Organic judging is text-only.
Each result records what Jev saw (`evidence`: `text-only`, `image` or `frames`) and its readings, in the suite
manifest and the Studio.

### Motion primitives

Every persona's `motionStyle` (smooth, snappy, liquid, mechanical) defines one motion language. The same language
writes the design tokens, the motion line in video prompts, and the options Jev chooses between when it reads a
loop. The language sets:

- **Curves**: `standard`, `enter` (decelerate), `exit` (accelerate), `emphasis`, and a physical spring
  (stiffness, damping, mass) exported as a CSS `linear()` curve with its settle time.
- **Distances, press and stagger**: nudge, shift and travel lengths, a press scale and a stagger interval. Dense
  personas move less and sequence faster.
- **Moves**: `enter`, `exit`, `hover`, `press`, `emphasis` and an `ambient` loop, as Web Animations keyframes
  with timing. The loop breathes for smooth personas, flickers for snappy, drifts for liquid and ticks for mechanical.

`baste tokens <id> --format css` ships them as variables (`--ease-enter`, `--ease-spring`, `--motion-shift`, …),
`@keyframes`, `.motion-enter`/`.motion-exit`/`.motion-hover`/`.motion-press`/`.motion-emphasis`/`.motion-ambient`
classes and `.motion-stagger` for sequences. A `prefers-reduced-motion` block keeps opacity-only enters and exits
and stops travel, emphasis and loops. The Tailwind and Panda exports carry the same curves, durations and keyframes,
and JSON carries the full choreography for animation libraries. The Studio's Tokens tab plays each move.

The callback is /api/notorganic/callback on the Studio origin. Production hosting must proxy /api to the Baste server. Sessions live in server memory and expire after eight hours; restarting the server requires signing in again. Read the account integration guide for the deployment boundary.

Use your own provider keys

Local mode keeps provider keys in the server environment or local config. Image generation uses OpenAI or Google; SVG generation uses QuiverAI; video uses its configured provider. The Studio never needs an upstream key pasted into a form.

Copy .env.example to .env and configure only the services you use. Run baste config --init to create baste.config.json. Model IDs must be supported by your chosen provider. Local generation and CLI use this configuration; hosted Studio requests use the connected account session.

Run everything on one fal key

With FAL_KEY set, one fal account can cover a whole run: Seedream v4 images, Recraft v3 vector icons, Seedance 1 Pro ambient loops, and a judge that looks at the rendered images through fal’s vision model. The archive in the tour came from a run like this.

--provider fal routes every stage through fal; --image-provider, --svg-provider, --video-provider and --judge override one stage each. The vision judge defaults to google/gemini-2.5-flash; SVG markup and video prompts go to the text endpoint because the vision endpoint needs an image. In the Studio, choose fal (images, icons and judge) as the image provider. A run fails at the start when FAL_KEY is missing, before anything is spent.

Draft with --dry-run first. Each stage bills your fal account, and judging adds a request for every candidate, so iterations and batch size multiply the cost.

Let Jev look

With TYPESAFE_API_KEY set, TypeSafe’s Jev judges every candidate and final asset, and it now judges what was rendered rather than the prompt. It sees each image, every SVG on light and dark grounds at 64, 32 and 16 px, and six frames sampled across each video loop. Beside them it gets up to four pictures of the persona’s world: moodboard pins, baste culture images, and a decomposed site’s share image and palette. It also sees the suite’s latest finished asset of each purpose, and the assets you upvoted and downvoted, which become pictured examples for a taste judgment.

In the same request, Jev reads the archive’s colour temperature, density and rendering off each image, so a candidate lands where it looks rather than where its prompt said it would. For images and loops, text laid over the picture (a caption, watermark or interface label) rejects the asset. Signs that belong to the scene do not. For loops, Jev names the motion it sees among the four motion languages, checks that the last frame flows into the first, and rates how calm the loop sits behind interface content. A miss becomes an improvement note, not a rejection.

Images are a TypeSafe preview feature: Baste sends the opt-in header and fits every picture inside TypeSafe’s limits first. Video frames, WebP and GIF need ffmpeg on the server; without it, those assets are judged on their prompt. If TypeSafe refuses an image request, that asset is judged again as text and tagged vision-refused. Hosted Not Organic judging stays text-only. Each result records what Jev saw as evidence: text-only, image or frames.

Motion primitives

A persona’s motion style (smooth, snappy, liquid or mechanical) is one motion language. It writes the motion tokens, the motion line in video prompts, and the options Jev chooses between when it reads a loop’s frames. Each language has semantic curves (standard, enter, exit, emphasis), a physical spring exported as a CSS linear() curve, travel distances, a press scale and a stagger interval. Denser personas move less and sequence faster.

content.text:
Jev now judges from pixels, and every image goes up as lossless PNG. AVIF isn't possible because TypeSafe only accepts PNG or JPEG. I haven't run any of this against live Jev: there's no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in your shell, `.envrc` or Skate. I tested it against a fake that follows TypeSafe's documented image rules. TypeSafe also labels images as a prototype ("Dreamer-ready") feature that may change.

**Images in Jev's decisions** (`src/evaluation/typesafe-judge.ts:424`)
- **The candidate:** Jev gets the rendered image instead of the prompt. SVGs are shown on light and dark backgrounds at full size and at 64, 32 and 16 px. Videos are sent as six frames from start to finish.
- **Style:** Jev also sees the latest finished asset of each purpose (up to four), so it compares against what was actually rendered rather than prompts.
- **Persona:** up to four pictures of the persona's world go in beside the candidate. They come from pinned moodboard images, `baste culture` images, and a decomposed site's share image and palette (`src/evaluation/visual-context.ts`).
- **Examples:** assets you upvoted and downvoted become pictured examples in a "closer to what you liked?" check. That moves persona alignment by up to ±0.1.
- **Extra checks from the same request:**
  - The search's three axes (colour temperature, density, how abstract) are now read from the image instead of guessed from prompt keywords.
  - Text laid over an image or loop (a caption, watermark or interface label) rejects it. Signs that belong to the scene don't count.
- **Fallbacks:** if TypeSafe refuses a request, Baste retries with the candidate image alone, then with text only, and tags the result. Use `--text-judge` (or `"vision": false` in config) to turn images off. Hosted Not Organic judging stays text-only.

**Motion** (`src/assets/motion.ts:180`)
- Each persona's motion style now has a fuller vocabulary:
  - curves for standard, enter, exit and emphasis
  - a real spring, exported as a CSS curve
  - travel distances, a press scale and a stagger interval (denser personas move less)
  - six ready-made moves: enter, exit, hover, press, emphasis, and an ambient loop
- **Exports:** CSS gets `.motion-*` classes, keyframes and a reduced-motion block. Tailwind and Panda get the same curves and keyframes; JSON carries everything for animation libraries.
- **Video prompts and Jev share it:** the same descriptions now drive video prompts and Jev's frame checks. Jev names which of the four styles a loop shows, checks the last frame flows into the first, and rates how calm it sits behind interface content. Misses become improvement notes, not rejections.
- **Bug fixed:** video prompts used to describe "mechanical" personas as "smooth".
- **Studio:** the Tokens tab's Motion panel plays each move.

**Checks:** 166 tests pass (138 before), and the site's typecheck, lint and tests pass. In Chrome, the exported CSS parses and animates, and reduced motion only fades. I checked the Motion panel at desktop width and 390 px. A full test run with fake providers sent images on all six Jev requests. The largest likely request is about 4.7 MB of TypeSafe's 32 MB limit.

**Worth knowing before you merge:**
- **Thresholds are guesses:** the text cut-off (0.8) and taste nudge (±0.1) are my settings, not tested values. Tune them after the first live run.
- **Archive changes:** reading the three axes from images will change which archive cell each candidate lands in.
- **ffmpeg:** video frames and fal's WebP images need `ffmpeg` on the machine running the API. Without it they're judged on their prompt.
- **Security fixes:** SVGs are cleaned so they can't pull local files into an uploaded image. Imported `.baste` files now drop local file paths from culture references, since those point at the sender's machine.
- **Not mine:** `site/src/components/fitting/fitting-room.tsx` changed during the session, but I didn't edit it.
- Nothing is committed.

# Ideogram API v2 Documentation Index

All API paths below sit under `https://developer.ideogram.ai/v2/api-reference/`. Adding `.md` to a page URL returns clean Markdown.

## Priority Summary: Ideogram 3 vs. Ideogram 4+

| Capability | Ideogram 3.0 | Ideogram 4.0 / 4.5 |
|---|---|---|
| Generate | `images/generate/ideogram-3.md` (plus character, custom, transparent variants) | `generate/ideogram-4.md`, `generate/ideogram-4-5.md` (plus 4.0 custom and transparent variants) |
| Inpaint / edit | `images/inpaint/ideogram-3.md` (plus character and custom variants) | 4.5 precise edit: `images/precise-edit/ideogram-4-5.md`. There is no inpaint page for v4. |
| Remix | `images/remix/ideogram-3.md` (plus character and custom variants) | `images/remix/ideogram-4.md` |
| Reframe | `images/reframe/ideogram-3.md` | None. Nano Banana 2 is the only other option. |
| Replace background | `images/replace-background/ideogram-3.md` | 4.5: `tool/replace-background-ideogram-45.md` |

| Describe | `images/describe/ideogram-3.md` | `images/describe/ideogram-4.md` |

**Gaps**
- No dedicated segmentation or matting endpoint exists. Remove-object (`images/remove-object/ideogram-1.md`) is the closest alternative.
- Your earlier notes say the edit docs don't state mask color semantics.

## Auth, Pricing and Rate Limits

| Topic | What the index offers |

| **Auth** | `ideogram-api/api-setup.md` covers dashboard access, billing setup and API key creation. `account/api-keys.md` lists keys. |
| **Pricing** | There's no dedicated pricing page. Credits are covered in API Setup. Spend data is in `account/usage.md` and `account/invoices.md`. |
| **Rate limits** | No page is listed. Try the OpenAPI spec (`/openapi.json` or `/openapi.yaml`) or the MCP server. |

**Docs**

# Ideogram 3.0 Replace Background: API Contract

## Endpoint
- **Method and URL:** `POST https://api.ideogram.ai/v2/image/replace-background/ideogram-3`
- **Content type:** `multipart/form-data`. The image must be uploaded as a file part.
- **Auth:** the `Api-Key` header is required.

## What it preserves
The subject is found automatically, so you don't send a mask. The page says the endpoint replaces the background while "keeping the automatically detected foreground subject; no mask is needed."

## Query parameter
- `dry_run` (boolean, default `false`): validates and prices the request without running it. In the page's words, "nothing is generated, stored, or billed, and no safety review is performed." It returns a `PriceQuote` object, whose schema isn't shown here.

## Body fields
| Field | Type | Req. | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | file | **yes** | Accepts JPEG, PNG, WEBP, HEIF, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF and MPO, up to 50 MB. Must be sent as multipart. |
| `prompt` | string | **yes** | "Plain-language description of the desired new background." |
| `rendering_speed` | enum | no | The allowed values aren't listed. |
| `num_images` | integer | no | No range or default is given. |
| `private` | boolean | no | "When omitted, defaults to your plan's setting. Enterprise generations are always private." |
| `webhook_url` | string | no | Must be HTTPS. Private, loopback and cloud-metadata hosts are rejected. |

## Constraints
- **Aspect ratio:** "The longer side must be at most 3 times the shorter side; wider aspect ratios are rejected with a 400."
- **File size:** 50 MB maximum.
- **Not available:** there is no `seed`, `mask`, `quality` or `async` field.

## Sync or async
The endpoint is **async only**. It "Returns a `generation_id`; poll `GET /v2/generations/{generation_id}` or supply a `webhook_url`."

**Webhook delivery:**
- "Ideogram sends a JSON POST to this URL once all images for the request have finished generating."
- The body contains `request_id`, `created` and `data[]`.
- Each item in `data[]` has `url`, `prompt`, `resolution`, `seed` and `is_image_safe`.
- Deliveries are signed with Ed25519. The public keys are at `https://api.ideogram.ai/v1/.well-known/jwks.json`.

## Response (200)
- The page describes this as "Background replacement accepted for asynchronous processing."
- The only field is `generation_id` (string, required).
- There's no `data` array and no `generation_kind`, unlike the Precise Edit endpoint from your earlier context.

## Errors
| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 400 | Invalid input, including an aspect ratio above 3:1 |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 402 | Insufficient credits or quota |
| 403 | Not authorized to replace backgrounds |
| 404 | Source image not found or not readable |
| 422 | Prompt failed safety checks |
| 429 | Too many requests |
| 503 | Temporarily unavailable |

The 402 and 429 bodies contain:
- `error`
- `reject_reason`: `insufficient_funds`, `subscription_required`, `daily_limit`, `priority_credit_required`, `inflight_limit` or `feature_limit`
- `max_inflight_requests` and `task_completion_speed` (`fast` or `slow`), present only when the reason is `inflight_limit`

## Gaps and caveats
- The output resolution isn't stated.
- The page doesn't say whether the foreground stays pixel-identical.
- The SDK samples are broken:
  - The Python sample passes the file as a quoted string and leaves values empty.
  - The PHP sample is missing a comma.
  - The Swift sample references an undefined `postData`.

## Endpoint
- **ID:** `fal-ai/ideogram/v3/replace-background`
- **Calls:**

  - `fal.queue.submit` returns a `request_id` and accepts an optional `webhookUrl`.
  - `fal.queue.status` and `fal.queue.result` take a `requestId`.
- **Auth:** set the `FAL_KEY` environment variable, or call `fal.config({ credentials })`.
- **Schema:** `/api/openapi/queue/openapi.json?endpoint_id=fal-ai/ideogram/v3/replace-background`

## Input
| Field | Type | Req. | Default / Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prompt` | string | **yes** | The page shows only an example: "Cyber punk city with neon lights and skyscrappers" |
| `image_url` | string | **yes** | "The image URL whose background needs to be replaced". Accepts a URL or a base64 data URI. |
| `rendering_speed` | enum | no | `BALANCED`. Options are `TURBO`, `BALANCED`, `QUALITY`. |
| `style` | enum | no | `AUTO`, `GENERAL`, `REALISTIC`, `DESIGN`. Can't be combined with `style_codes`. |
| `style_preset` | enum | no | About 60 presets, from `80S_ILLUSTRATION` to `WOODBLOCK_PRINT`. |
| `style_codes` | list\<string> | no | 8-character hex codes. Can't be combined with `style` or style references. |
| `image_urls` | list\<string> | no | Style reference images in JPEG, PNG or WebP, "maximum total size 10MB across all style references" |
| `color_palette` | ColorPalette | no | Either a preset `name` or a list of `members`. |
| `expand_prompt` | boolean | no | `true` (turns on MagicPrompt) |
| `num_images` | integer | no | `1` |
| `seed` | integer | no | None |
| `sync_mode` | boolean | no | When true, the output comes back as a data URI and is left out of request history. |

**Supporting types:**
- **ColorPalette:** `name` (one of `EMBER`, `FRESH`, `JUNGLE`, `MAGIC`, `MELON`, `MOSAIC`, `PASTEL`, `ULTRAMARINE`) or `members` (a list of ColorPaletteMember).
- **ColorPaletteMember:** `rgb` (RGBColor, required) and `color_weight` (float, default `0.5`).
- **RGBColor:** integers `r`, `g`, `b`.

**Documentation quirk:** the `style_codes` note refers to "style_reference_images", but the input field is actually named `image_urls`.

## Output
- `images`: list\<File>, required. Each File has:
  - `url` (required)
  - `content_type`
  - `file_name`
  - `file_size`
- `seed`: integer, required.

- **On this fal page:** none. Reframe, remix, edit and generate/transparent are not mentioned, and the "Related Models" section is empty.

  - `POST /v2/image/reframe/ideogram-3` is multipart, takes no prompt, and requires `resolution`.
  - `POST /v2/image/replace-background/ideogram-3` is multipart and async-only. It takes `image` and `prompt`, and has no `seed`.

| `end_image_url` | string or null | none | none | Optional final frame: "The URL of the image the video ends with. Defaults to None." |
| `duration` | string | `"5"` | `"2"` to `"12"` (every whole number in between, as strings) | Video length in seconds. |
| `num_frames` | integer or null | none | 29–289 | Number of frames to generate. "If provided, will override duration." |
| `resolution` | string | `"1080p"` | `480p`, `720p`, `1080p` | 480p is fastest, 720p is the middle option, 1080p gives the highest quality. |

- **`video`** (File): the generated video. Example URL: `.../seedance_pro_i2v.mp4`
  - `url` (string, required)
  - `content_type` (string or null)
  - `file_name` (string or null)
  - `file_size` (integer or null, in bytes)
- **`seed`** (integer): the seed used for generation. Example: `42`.

## Queue Endpoints

- **Server:** `https://queue.fal.run`
- **Auth:** `Authorization` header containing your Fal Key.
- **Calls:**
  - `POST /fal-ai/bytedance/seedance/v1/pro/image-to-video` submits a request and returns a QueueStatus.
  - `GET .../requests/{request_id}/status` checks progress. Add `logs=1` to include logs.
  - `PUT .../requests/{request_id}/cancel` cancels a request.
  - `GET .../requests/{request_id}` returns the result.
- **QueueStatus `status` values:** `IN_QUEUE`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`.

result.output:
# Upload Flow in the fal Storage Client (`storage.js`)

## 1. Initiate request (single upload)

- **Method and URL:** `method: "POST",` and
  "`targetUrl: `${(0, config_1.getRestApiUrl)()}/storage/upload/initiate?storage_type=fal-cdn-v3`,`"
- **Body fields:** "`content_type: contentType,`" and "`file_name: filename,`"
- **Filename fallback:** "`const filename = file.name || `${Date.now()}.${getExtensionFromContentType(contentType)}`;`"
- **Optional lifecycle header:** "`headers["X-Fal-Object-Lifecycle"] = JSON.stringify(lifecycleConfig);`"
  - The JSON can contain `expiration_duration_seconds` and/or `initial_acl`.
- **Transport:** the request is sent with `request_1.dispatchRequest`, passing `config` and `headers`.

## 2. Response fields used

"`const { upload_url: uploadUrl, file_url: url } = yield initiateUpload(file, config, contentType, lifecycle);`"

## 3. PUT upload

- "`const response = yield fetch(uploadUrl, {`"
- "`method: "PUT",`" and "`body: file,`"
- "`"Content-Type": file.type || "application/octet-stream",`"

After the PUT, the response goes through `responseHandler`, and the function returns `url`, which is the `file_url`.

## 4. Multipart threshold and chunking

- **Threshold:** "`if (file.size > 90 * 1024 * 1024) {`"
- **Initiate endpoint:** "`/storage/upload/initiate-multipart?storage_type=fal-cdn-v3`". The body and headers match the single-upload case.
- **Chunk size:** "`const chunkSize = 10 * 1024 * 1024;`"
- **Part URL:** "`const partUploadUrl = `${parsedUrl.origin}${parsedUrl.pathname}/${partNumber}${parsedUrl.search}`;`"
- **Part upload:** each part is sent with PUT and retried up to 3 times ("`tries = 3`").
- **Completion URL:** "`const completeUrl = `${parsedUrl.origin}${parsedUrl.pathname}/complete${parsedUrl.search}`;`"
- **Completion request:** a POST with JSON `{ parts: [{ partNumber, etag }] }`.

## 5. `getRestApiUrl`

This file does not define it. It is only imported: "`const config_1 = require("./config");`". As a result, the actual host is not visible in this content.

## 6. `transformInput` auto-upload

- **Arrays:** each element is transformed recursively.
- **Blobs:** "`else if (input instanceof Blob) {`" followed by "`return yield ref.upload(input);`"
- **Plain objects:** each value is transformed recursively.
- **Everything else** is returned unchanged.

**Data URIs:** a comment mentions them ("`neither an object nor a file/blob/data URI`"). However, this file contains no code that parses or uploads data-URI strings, so only `Blob`/`File` values are uploaded automatically.

input.content:
# Edit, layer and animate: SAM + Ideogram + persona animation

## Context

Baste creates images with one model (GPT Image by default) and then only judges them. The user wants:
- **Separate models for creating and editing.** GPT Image creates; Ideogram edits.
- **Segment Anything** to pull a subject from its background, so backgrounds and foregrounds can be rebuilt and edited during generation.
- **Animations built from those layers, described in the persona.**

Decisions (asked in plan mode):
- Ideogram goes **through fal** on the existing `FAL_KEY`.
- **Both** parallax loops (from layers) and image-to-video loops.
- Edits happen **inside QD as well as on final assets**.
- **Studio UI** is in scope this round.

Verified contracts (fal OpenAPI):
- **`fal-ai/sam-3/image`**:
  - inputs: `image_url`, text `prompt`, `apply_mask`, `return_multiple_masks`, `max_masks`, `include_scores`, `include_boxes`
  - output: `masks[]` plus `metadata[{index, score, box (normalized cx,cy,w,h)}]`
- **`fal-ai/ideogram/v3/edit`**:
  - inputs: `prompt`, `image_url`, `mask_url`; the mask must match the image size exactly
  - also: `rendering_speed`, `style_preset`, `image_urls` style references (≤10 MB), `color_palette`
  - Ideogram's own docs: **black = edit, white = keep**. fal's page doesn't say; a live check is needed.
- **`fal-ai/bytedance/seedance/v1/pro/image-to-video`**:
  - inputs: `image_url`, `end_image_url`, `duration` "2"–"12", `resolution`, `camera_fixed`
- **fal upload**: POST `https://rest.fal.ai/storage/upload/initiate?storage_type=fal-cdn-v3` `{content_type,file_name}` with `Authorization: Key` returns `{upload_url,file_url}`; then PUT the bytes to `upload_url` without the key.
- **resvg** (already a dependency) handles every mask job in memory: luminance-mask cut-outs, `feMorphology` dilation, inversion and feathering. No new image library is needed.

## Design

### 1. Persona animation (`src/persona/types.ts`)
- Add optional `animation?: PersonaAnimation` with these fields:
  - `motifs`: what moves in their world
  - `subjects`: things that can stand as a separate front layer
  - `depth`: `flat|parallax|deep`
  - `camera`: `locked|drift|push|orbit`
  - `focus`: `background|subject|both`
  - `loopSeconds`
  - `avoid`: motion they can't stand
- New `animationFor(persona)` in `src/assets/motion.ts`:
  - fills a missing block from the aesthetic (motion style → camera, density → depth)
  - takes `loopSeconds` from the motion tokens' ambient length (6 / 4 / 9 / 12 s), clamped to Seedance's 2–12 s
- Thread the field through:
  - `src/projects/schemas.ts` strict zod (**rejects unknown keys today**)
  - `src/persona/builder.ts`: `PersonaDraft`, `buildPersona` and `extendPersona` (**currently drop it**; merge lists with `mergeUnique`)
  - the three base personas in `src/persona/base-personas.ts`, with authored blocks:
    - cyberbotanist: spores and bioluminescent pulses, mushrooms and ferns, deep, drift
    - nightmarketcoder: neon flicker and wok steam, lanterns and stalls, parallax, locked, both
    - liminalweeb: humming fluorescents and empty escalators, mannequins and fountains, deep, push
  - `src/cli.ts` `show`
  - `src/mcp/server.ts` `create_persona`: optional `animation` arg
  - `site/src/lib/api-types.ts`
- Video prompts (`src/generation/prompts.ts`) and Jev's frame questions use the motifs and the avoid list. Add one Noul, "does the motion include anything in `persona.animation.avoid`?", whose answer becomes an improvement note.

### 2. Separate roles in config (`src/config/baste-config.ts`, `src/assets/generators.ts` `GenerationConfig`)
- Under `generators`, add:
  - `edit`: `{provider:"fal", model:"fal-ai/ideogram/v3/edit", renderingSpeed}`
  - `segment`: `{provider:"fal", model:"fal-ai/sam-3/image"}`
  - `animate`: `{provider:"fal", model:"fal-ai/bytedance/seedance/v1/pro/image-to-video", resolution}`
- `image` stays the creation model. All three share `falApiKey`.
- Run switches, off by default so existing runs cost what they cost today:
  - CLI: `--edit` and `--animate <parallax|video|both>`
  - GUI request: `edit?: boolean` and `animate?`
- `--animate` implies segmentation.
- `src/assets/fal.ts`: add `falUpload(bytes, contentType, key)` (the key goes only to `rest.fal.ai`; the PUT carries no key; the returned `file_url` is checked with `falMediaUrl`). Images that already came from fal reuse their `metadata.sourceUrl`.

### 3. Segment and layer (new `src/assets/layers.ts`)
- **`segmentSubject(imagePath, persona)`**:
  - Calls SAM 3 for each candidate subject in turn: `persona.animation.subjects`, then nouns from the prompt, then generic "main subject".
  - Settings: `apply_mask:false`, `include_scores:true`, `max_masks:3`.
  - Accepts a mask with score ≥ 0.5 that covers 3–70% of the frame, measured from resvg pixels.
  - When Jev is configured, a **Jev Choice over the pictured subject list** picks which subject is in the image first. This is TypeSafe's "select instead of generate" pattern.
  - Masks are normalized to white-on-black at the source size.
  - Results are cached per source path as `Map<path, Promise<…>>`, so parallel QD children share them.
- **`buildLayers(asset, persona, cfg)`** writes `assets/output/layers/<id>-{fg,bg,mask}.png`:
  - **fg**: the subject cut out with a 1.5 px feathered alpha
  - **bg**: Ideogram edit with a mask dilated about 2% of the short side and inverted (black = edit), prompted to continue the background with no subject and persona style cues
  - **mask**: the subject mask
- Flat filenames keep the GUI's `^[\w.-]+$` asset route safe.

### 4. QD edit children (`src/baste.ts`, `src/generation/qd.ts`, `src/generation/prompts.ts`)
- The genome becomes `ImageGenome {prompt; path?; sourceUrl?; edit?: {from; layer: "background"|"subject"; instruction; axis; step}}`.
  - Swap `string` for it at `baste.ts:73/144/149`.
  - Use `.prompt` at `:175`, `:192` and `:275`.
- `runQD` stays generic: `evaluate` may return `genome` with the rendered path, and `runQD` stores that version.
- **Mutation**: when `--edit` is on and the parent has a `path`, about half the children are edits:
  - The layer comes from `persona.animation.focus`.
  - A new exported `axisStep()` (factored out of `stepAxis`) returns `{prompt, axis, from, to}`.
  - The instruction reads like "Repaint the background in deep ember orange and red, keep the lantern untouched". The child's prompt is the stepped prompt.
- **Evaluation**: an edit child segments its parent (cached), then sends it to Ideogram. The judge's prompt gets an `Edit:` line.
- **Final step reuses the judged image** (`solution.genome.path`) instead of regenerating. This is a behaviour change: shipped pixels equal judged pixels, and it saves one image call per output. `tests/fal.test.ts:173` expects 3 calls → 2.
- `markCells` matches on the path. Candidates carry optional `edit` lineage (`QDCandidate`, `CandidateSummary`, `gui/api.ts:363`).

### 5. Animations (new `src/assets/animate.ts`)
All outputs land in `assets/output/animation/`.
- **Parallax**, built from layers:
  - `<id>-parallax.json`: layer spec with depth factors, camera path, loop length and easing from the motion tokens
  - `<id>-parallax.html`: self-contained; data-URI layers, CSS `@keyframes` only, **no script**, and a `prefers-reduced-motion` stop
  - `<id>-parallax.mp4`: rendered by ffmpeg `overlay`/`crop` with `sin(2πt/T)` paths, so the first and last frames match exactly
  - Depth sets the background/foreground ratio. Camera sets the path: drift pans, push zooms, orbit circles, locked lets only the subject breathe. Amplitudes come from the motion tokens' travel distance.
- **Video**, built from edits:
  - The end frame is an Ideogram edit of the final image, showing the persona's motif at its peak, masked to `focus` (`<id>-end.png`).
  - Seedance image-to-video runs from the start frame to the end frame (`<id>-transition.mp4`).
  - ffmpeg plays it forward then reversed to make a seamless `<id>-loop.mp4`.
  - `camera_fixed` is set when camera is `locked`. Jev judges the loop's frames: motion style, seam, calm and avoid list.
- Without ffmpeg there is no parallax MP4 and no ping-pong loop; the HTML, the JSON and the Seedance transition are still produced.

### 6. Suite wiring

# Edit, layer and animate: SAM + Ideogram + persona animation

## Context

Baste creates images with one model (GPT Image by default) and then only judges them. The user wants:
- **Separate models for creating and editing.** GPT Image creates; Ideogram edits.
- **Segment Anything** to split a subject from its background, so foregrounds and backgrounds can be edited during generation.
- **Animations built from those pieces, defined in the persona.**

Decisions made in planning:
- Ideogram runs **through fal**, on the existing `FAL_KEY`.
- **Both** parallax loops and image-to-video loops.
- Edits happen **inside QD as well as on final assets**.
- **Studio UI** is in scope this round.

Verified fal contracts:
- **`fal-ai/sam-3/image`**:
  - inputs: `image_url` (URL or base64 data URI), text `prompt`, `apply_mask`, `return_multiple_masks`, `max_masks`, `include_scores`, `include_boxes`
  - output: `masks[]` and `metadata[{index, score, box}]`
- **`fal-ai/ideogram/v3/edit`**:
  - inputs: `prompt`, `image_url`, `mask_url`; the mask must have the image's exact size
  - also: `rendering_speed`, `style_preset`, `image_urls` (style references, at most 10 MB total), `color_palette`
  - Ideogram's own API: **black = edit, white = keep**. fal doesn't say, so a live check settles it.
- **`fal-ai/bytedance/seedance/v1/pro/image-to-video`**: `image_url`, `end_image_url`, `duration` "2"–"12", `resolution`, `camera_fixed`.
- **fal upload**: POST `rest.fal.ai/storage/upload/initiate?storage_type=fal-cdn-v3` with `Authorization: Key …`, which returns `{upload_url, file_url}`; then PUT the bytes with no key.
- **resvg**, already a dependency, does every mask job in memory: luminance cut-outs, `feMorphology` dilation, inversion and feathering (all tested).

## Design

### 1. Persona animation
- **Type** (`src/persona/types.ts`): optional `animation?: PersonaAnimation`, with:
  - `motifs`: what moves in their world
  - `subjects`: things that can be cut out as a front layer
  - `depth`: `flat|parallax|deep`
  - `camera`: `locked|drift|push|orbit`
  - `focus`: `background|subject|both`
  - `loopSeconds`
  - `avoid`: motion they can't stand
- **Defaults** (`src/assets/motion.ts`): `animationFor(persona)` fills any missing parts from the aesthetic:
  - motion style sets the camera, density sets the depth
  - loop length comes from the ambient loop (6, 4, 9 or 12 s), clamped to Seedance's 2–12 s
- **Threading** (validation currently rejects or drops the field):
  - `src/projects/schemas.ts`: strict zod rejects unknown keys; add `animation` to it **first**
  - `src/persona/builder.ts`: `PersonaDraft`, `buildPersona` and `extendPersona` drop it today; merge it, combining lists with `mergeUnique`
  - Remix (`gui/api.ts:1015`, `mcp/server.ts:487`, `cli.ts:530`) keeps it once the builder is fixed
  - `src/mcp/server.ts` `create_persona`: add an optional `animation` argument
  - `src/cli.ts` `show`, and `site/src/lib/api-types.ts`
- **Authored blocks** for the three base personas:
  - cyberbotanist: spores and bioluminescent pulses; mushrooms and ferns; deep; drift
  - nightmarketcoder: neon flicker and wok steam; lanterns and stalls; parallax; locked; both
  - liminalweeb: humming fluorescents and empty escalators; mannequins and a fountain; deep; push
- **Prompts and Jev**: video prompts use the motifs and the avoid list. Jev's loop judgment adds one Noul, "does the motion include anything in `persona.animation.avoid`?". A yes becomes an improvement note.

### 2. Separate roles in config
In `src/config/baste-config.ts` and `GenerationConfig`, `generators` gains three roles beside `image`, which stays the creation model. All three share `falApiKey`:
- `edit`: `fal-ai/ideogram/v3/edit`, at `BALANCED` speed
- `segment`: `fal-ai/sam-3/image`
- `animate`: `fal-ai/bytedance/seedance/v1/pro/image-to-video`, at `720p`

New controls, off by default so normal runs cost what they did:
- CLI flags `--edit` and `--animate <parallax|video|both>`; `--animate` implies segmenting
- GUI request fields `edit` and `animate`
- Hosted Not Organic runs reject both, because direct fal calls would bypass its budget

For image inputs, `falImageInput(path)` in `src/assets/fal.ts` picks one of three:
- the asset's `metadata.sourceUrl`, if it is already hosted on fal
- a data URI, if the file is 4 MiB or less (masks always qualify)
- otherwise `falUpload` (the key goes only to `rest.fal.ai`, and the returned URL is checked with `falMediaUrl`)

### 3. Segment and layer (new `src/assets/layers.ts`)
- **Choosing the subject (a Jev fan-out)**:
  - When edit or animate is on, Jev's judgment request already holds the candidate image, so it also asks a `mainSubject` Choice. The options are the persona's subjects plus `none`.
  - SAM's text prompt is the chosen subject. Without Jev, Baste tries the subjects in order.
  - A mask is accepted when its score is at least 0.5 and it covers 3–70% of the frame.
  - When nothing qualifies, there is **no edit**: the child is regenerated instead, so a background edit never repaints the whole frame.
- **Masks**: `subjectMask` resizes SAM's output to the source's exact size, read from the PNG header (`parseImageDimensions`), never from the requested ratio. One helper, `editMask(subject, region)`, does both cases:
  - background region: the inverse of the subject dilated by about 2% (black = edit)
  - subject region: the subject itself, slightly dilated

  Each case gets its own unit test.
- **Cache**: a per-path `Map<path, Promise>`, so concurrent QD children share one SAM call. A failed lookup is removed from the map so it can be retried.
- **`buildLayers`** writes `output/layers/<id>-{fg,bg,mask}.png`:
  - `fg`: the subject on transparency, with a 1.5 px feathered edge
  - `bg`: an Ideogram edit that continues the background with the subject removed and the persona's style kept
  - Ideogram's result is resized back to the source size so the layers line up.
- **Cut check**: one Jev request with two Nouls, "is the subject whole?" and "is the plate free of it?". A failed cut is dropped and logged instead of shipped. This only runs when Jev is configured.

### 4. Edit children in QD (`src/generation/qd.ts`, `src/baste.ts`, `src/generation/prompts.ts`)
- **`runQD`**: `evaluate` returns `{quality, features, genome?}`, and the archive stores `evaluation.genome ?? child.genome` for both seeds and children. The engine stays generic.
- **Genome type**: `ImageGenome = { prompt; asset?: GeneratedAsset; edit?: { from; layer; instruction; axis; step } }`. Change every `string` use in `baste.ts`: `:73`, `:144`, `:149`, `:163`, `:175`, `:192`, `:275` and `:359-360`.
- **Mutation**:
  - With `--edit` and a parent that has an image and a subject, about half the children are edits, capped at `iterations × ceil(batchSize/2)` per run.
  - The counter is checked synchronously, so it is safe under `Promise.all`.
  - A new exported `axisStep()`, factored out of `stepAxis`, gives the axis step and an instruction such as "Repaint the background in deep ember orange and red; keep the lantern untouched".
  - The child's prompt is the stepped prompt, so later prompt mutations stay consistent.
- **Evaluation**: an edit child segments its parent (cached), runs the Ideogram edit, and adds an `Edit:` line to the judge's prompt.
- **Final step**:
  - When the first image asset's archive solution has an image, Baste ships it instead of regenerating. That saves one image call per output, and what ships is exactly what was judged.
  - Other image assets still regenerate from their own prompts.
  - The final judge still runs, now comparing against the rendered suite.
  - `tests/fal.test.ts:173` changes from 3 to 2 text-to-image calls.
- **Cell matching and lineage**: `markCells` matches on the asset path instead of quality plus float features. Candidates carry optional `edit` lineage (`QDCandidate`, `CandidateSummary`, `gui/api.ts:363`).

### 5. Animations (new `src/assets/animate.ts`, output to `output/animation/`)
- **Parallax** (core output, from the layers):
  - `<id>-parallax.json`: the layer spec (depth factors, camera path, loop length and the persona's motion easing)
  - `<id>-parallax.html`: self-contained, with layers as data URIs, CSS `@keyframes` only, **no script**, and a reduced-motion stop
  - Depth sets the foreground/background ratio. Camera sets the move: drift pans, push zooms, orbit circles, and locked lets only the subject breathe. Amplitudes come from the travel token.
  - With ffmpeg, also `<id>-parallax.mp4`, rendered from `sin(2πt/T)` paths so the first frame equals the last.
- **Video** (built last):
  - an Ideogram edit of the final image showing the persona's motif at its peak, masked to `focus` (`<id>-end.png`)
  - Seedance image-to-video from the start frame to that end frame (`camera_fixed` when the camera is locked)
  - with ffmpeg, a forward-then-reversed `<id>-loop.mp4`
  - Jev judges the loop's frames: motion style, seam, calm, avoid list

### 6. Suite, manifest, API
- **Suite** (`generateAssetSuite`): after final assets, each image gains optional `layers` and `animation` paths. `assets.{svgs,images,videos}` keep their shape.
- **Manifest** (`cli.ts` `manifestAsset`): carries the new paths.
- **Asset route** (`gui/api.ts:1182`): the regex gains the `layers` and `animation` kinds. The type map gains `html` and `json`. HTML is served with `CSP: sandbox; default-src 'none'; img-src data:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'` plus `nosniff`. The hosted rule still serves raster images only; a test confirms it returns 404 for the new kinds.
- **Logs**: the CLI and job logs state the number of edits and segmentations before spending.

### 7. Studio
- **Generate tab** (local runs):
  - an "Edit with Ideogram" toggle and an Animate choice (off, parallax, video or both), each with a cost hint
  - results add a layer strip (cut-out on a checkerboard, plate, mask) and a parallax preview (the MP4, or the HTML in a script-less `sandbox` iframe)
  - results add the video loop and download links; `AssetCaption` takes extra links
- **Persona form**: a "How their world moves" section (motifs, subjects and avoid as lists; depth, camera and focus as chips; loop length). Tailoring keeps `source.animation`, which it drops today.
- **Demo data**: regenerated. Replay is unaffected because the new keys are optional and guarded.

### 8. Docs
- **README**: an "Edit, layer and animate" section, with a table of roles (create, edit, segment, animate), the flags, the outputs and the hosted limit.
- **Developer docs page**: the matching section.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: the services line.

## Order and live checks
After each step the tests are green.
1. Correct the memory note `jev-vision-unverified.md`: the TypeSafe, fal, OpenAI and QuiverAI keys are in Skate `@secrets`.
2. Persona `animation`, config roles and flags.
3. The `runQD` genome change and final-image reuse, on their own, including the `fal.test.ts` update.
4. `falImageInput`, SAM, masks and the cut check.
5. QD edit children. Then **live check A**: SAM and one Ideogram edit on an existing fitting image, about $0.10, to settle mask polarity and size.
6. Parallax JSON, HTML and MP4, plus the asset route.
7. Seedance end-frame loop.
8. Studio.
9. Docs.
10. **Live check B**: `baste generate nightmarketcoder` with a hero-only config, `--edit --animate both --iterations 1 --batch-size 2 --output-count 1 --judge typesafe`, at 720p, an estimated $1–3. Keys are read from Skate.

## Verification
- **Unit tests** with the fake fal from `tests/fal.test.ts`, covering:
  - `falImageInput`: all three branches, and the key never leaving `rest.fal.ai`/the queue
  - the SAM request shape, the subject fallback and the 3–70% coverage gate
  - `editMask` polarity in both cases, with output sized exactly to the source
  - the foreground's alpha
  - Ideogram resized back to the source size
  - edit children calling the edit endpoint, with the cap respected
  - the final image reused and lineage recorded
  - the cut check dropping a bad cut
  - the parallax HTML: no `<script`, data images only, reduced-motion block
  - the parallax MP4: the loop's length, first frame ≈ last
  - Seedance receiving `end_image_url`, with the ping-pong loop doubling the length
  - `personaSchema` accepting and rejecting `animation`, and `extendPersona` and remix keeping `avoid`
  - the asset route: CSP, path traversal, hosted 404
  - hosted runs rejecting `edit` and `animate`
- **Suites**: `npm test`, plus the site's typecheck, lint and tests.
- **Studio QA** in Chrome at desktop and 390 px: the generate toggles, layer strip, parallax preview and persona form section.
- **Live checks A and B** (above): inspect the layers and loops by eye, and report the requests made and the estimated spend.

  - A new exported `axisStep()`, factored out of `stepAxis`, gives the axis step and an instruction such as "Repaint the background in deep ember orange and red; keep the lantern untouched".

- **Evaluation**: an edit child segments its parent (cached), runs the Ideogram edit, and adds an `Edit:` line to the judge's prompt.
- **Final step**:
  - When the first image asset's archive solution has an image, Baste ships it instead of regenerating. That saves one image call per output, and what ships is exactly what was judged.
  - Other image assets still regenerate from their own prompts.
  - The final judge still runs, now comparing against the rendered suite.
  - `tests/fal.test.ts:173` changes from 3 to 2 text-to-image calls.
- **Cell matching and lineage**: `markCells` matches on the asset path instead of quality plus float features. Candidates carry optional `edit` lineage (`QDCandidate`, `CandidateSummary`, `gui/api.ts:363`).

### 5. Animations (new `src/assets/animate.ts`, output to `output/animation/`)
- **Parallax** (core output, from the layers):
  - `<id>-parallax.json`: the layer spec (depth factors, camera path, loop length and the persona's motion easing)
  - `<id>-parallax.html`: self-contained, with layers as data URIs, CSS `@keyframes` only, **no script**, and a reduced-motion stop
  - Depth sets the foreground/background ratio. Camera sets the move: drift pans, push zooms, orbit circles, and locked lets only the subject breathe. Amplitudes come from the travel token.
  - With ffmpeg, also `<id>-parallax.mp4`, rendered from `sin(2πt/T)` paths so the first frame equals the last.
- **Video** (built last):
  - an Ideogram edit of the final image showing the persona's motif at its peak, masked to `focus` (`<id>-end.png`)
  - Seedance image-to-video from the start frame to that end frame (`camera_fixed` when the camera is locked)
  - with ffmpeg, a forward-then-reversed `<id>-loop.mp4`
  - Jev judges the loop's frames: motion style, seam, calm, avoid list

### 6. Suite, manifest, API
- **Suite** (`generateAssetSuite`): after final assets, each image gains optional `layers` and `animation` paths. `assets.{svgs,images,videos}` keep their shape.
- **Manifest** (`cli.ts` `manifestAsset`): carries the new paths.
- **Asset route** (`gui/api.ts:1182`): the regex gains the `layers` and `animation` kinds. The type map gains `html` and `json`. HTML is served with `CSP: sandbox; default-src 'none'; img-src data:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'` plus `nosniff`. The hosted rule still serves raster images only; a test confirms it returns 404 for the new kinds.
- **Logs**: the CLI and job logs state the number of edits and segmentations before spending.

### 7. Studio
- **Generate tab** (local runs):
  - an "Edit with Ideogram" toggle and an Animate choice (off, parallax, video or both), each with a cost hint
  - results add a layer strip (cut-out on a checkerboard, plate, mask) and a parallax preview (the MP4, or the HTML in a script-less `sandbox` iframe)
  - results add the video loop and download links; `AssetCaption` takes extra links
- **Persona form**: a "How their world moves" section (motifs, subjects and avoid as lists; depth, camera and focus as chips; loop length). Tailoring keeps `source.animation`, which it drops today.
- **Demo data**: regenerated. Replay is unaffected because the new keys are optional and guarded.

### 8. Docs
- **README**: an "Edit, layer and animate" section, with a table of roles (create, edit, segment, animate), the flags, the outputs and the hosted limit.
- **Developer docs page**: the matching section.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: the services line.

After each step the tests are green.

8. Studio.

- **Unit tests** with the fake fal from `tests/fal.test.ts`, covering:
  - `falImageInput`: all three branches, and the key never leaving `rest.fal.ai`/the queue
  - the SAM request shape, the subject fallback and the 3–70% coverage gate

  - the parallax MP4: the loop's length, first frame ≈ last

- **Suites**: `npm test`, plus the site's typecheck, lint and tests.

### Motion primitives

Every persona's `motionStyle` (smooth, snappy, liquid, mechanical) defines one motion language. The same language
writes the design tokens, the motion line in video prompts, and the options Jev chooses between when it reads a
loop. The language sets:

- **Curves**: `standard`, `enter` (decelerate), `exit` (accelerate), `emphasis`, and a physical spring
  (stiffness, damping, mass) exported as a CSS `linear()` curve with its settle time.
- **Distances, press and stagger**: nudge, shift and travel lengths, a press scale and a stagger interval. Dense
  personas move less and sequence faster.
- **Moves**: `enter`, `exit`, `hover`, `press`, `emphasis` and an `ambient` loop, as Web Animations keyframes
  with timing. The loop breathes for smooth personas, flickers for snappy, drifts for liquid and ticks for mechanical.

`baste tokens <id> --format css` ships them as variables (`--ease-enter`, `--ease-spring`, `--motion-shift`, …),

---
name: jev-vision-unverified
description: Jev image judging, SAM 3 and Ideogram edits are verified live (2026-10-18); provider keys are in Skate @secrets; fal's Ideogram repaints mask WHITE
metadata:
  type: project
---

Live runs on 2026-10-18, using keys from Skate `@secrets`, confirmed the following:
- **Jev:**
  - Jev judges real images and video frames over multipart.
  - It read a Seedance loop as the nightmarketcoder's own "snappy" motion style (83%), with a smooth seam (0.77).
- **SAM 3** (`fal-ai/sam-3/image`):
  - It returns white-on-black PNG masks at the source size, with one mask per instance.
  - Baste merges the instances; nightmarketcoder's scattered lanterns covered 3% of the frame.
- **fal's Ideogram v3 edit:**
  - It repaints the mask's **white** and keeps the black. This is the opposite of Ideogram's own API docs.
  - Measured mean change was 64 on white versus 15 on black. `EDIT_COLOR = "white"` in `src/assets/layers.ts` encodes this.
  - It returns about 2× upscaled images. Baste resizes them back to the source size.
- **Seedance i2v with `end_image_url`:**
  - Repainting a background that fills most of the frame (88%) invents a new scene, and the loop morphs between two places.
  - Baste therefore caps end-frame repaints at half the frame (`MAX_END_REPAINT`).

Key names: `typesafe_api_key`, `fal_api_key`, `openai-api`, `quiverai_api_key`. Read them with `skate get <name>@secrets`; plain `skate list` doesn't show them.

**Why:** These preview APIs changed behaviour against their docs. Mask polarity is easy to get wrong silently.
**How to apply:** If edits start changing the subject instead of the background, re-measure polarity on one image before flipping `EDIT_COLOR`. Still not tuned against real answers: the text threshold (0.8), taste weight (±0.1) and cut-check thresholds (0.5).

content.text:
Edit, segment and animate are built, and each fal model (SAM 3, Ideogram and Seedance) and Jev has been called live at least once. The one exception: edits inside the search across several generations have only run against a fake. Nothing is committed.

**What you asked for**
- **Separate models for creating and editing:** your image model still creates. Ideogram 3 edits, SAM 3 cuts out subjects, and Seedance makes video loops. All run on your `FAL_KEY` and are configured separately under `generators.edit`, `generators.segment` and `generators.animate`.
- **SAM-driven edits during generation (`--edit`):**
  - About half of each generation's new candidates repaint a kept candidate's background or subject instead of drawing a new image. Each repaint moves one step along the archive's axes (`src/baste.ts:194`).
  - Jev judges edits like any other candidate, and each records which image it came from.
  - Every final image is cut into three layers: the subject on transparency, the scene with the subject painted out, and the mask. Jev picks which of the persona's subjects to cut and checks that the cut is clean.
- **Animation in the persona:** personas have an optional `animation` block: what moves, subjects that can be cut out, depth, camera, focus, loop length and motion to avoid. The three built-in personas have one written; other personas get one derived from their aesthetic. `--animate parallax|video|both` makes the loops (`src/assets/animate.ts`):
  - **Parallax:** the layers move at different depths along the persona's camera. It ships as an HTML page with no scripts, a JSON spec, and an MP4 that loops exactly.
  - **Video:** Seedance animates the image, played forward then back so it loops.
- **Studio:** the Generate tab has edit and animate controls, and results show the layers and both loops. The persona form has a "How their world moves" section. I checked these in Chrome at desktop width and 390 px, using results from a real run.

**What the live runs showed** (roughly $1 in calls by my estimate; I didn't check the invoices)
- **fal's Ideogram repaints a mask's white, not its black,** the opposite of Ideogram's own docs. My first test edit repainted the lanterns instead of keeping them. After flipping it (`EDIT_COLOR`, `src/assets/layers.ts:73`), the background changed 7× more than the subject.
- **SAM returns one mask per lantern.** I merge them into one layer; otherwise small repeated subjects never qualified.
- **Large end frames break the video loop:** repainting a background that fills most of the frame made it morph between two different markets. End frames now repaint only regions under half the frame; for the night market, that's just the lanterns.
- **Jev's motion reading varies:** it read the first loop as the persona's own snappy style (83%). It read the second as mechanical and added an improvement note.
- **The real cut was clean:** Jev's check passed the cut-out and background of the real hero.

**Behaviour changes**
- The final step ships the image the search judged instead of drawing it again. That's one fewer image call per output. It also lowers the hosted spending cap for the default suite from $14.40 to $12.90; the docs and tests are updated.
- Hosted Not Organic runs reject `--edit` and `--animate`, because those calls go straight to fal, outside the account's budget.

**Not yet verified**
- No live `--edit` run across several generations. The live checks covered single edits, layers and both loops.
- These thresholds are my guesses, not tuned values:
  - Jev's cut check passes at 0.5 or above.
  - SAM masks need a score of at least 0.5.
  - A cut-out must cover 2–70% of the frame.

All 182 tests pass, 16 of them new. The site's typecheck, lint and tests also pass.
